name: read-back
wording: What a party hands the operator at a gate: where things stand, in plain words, as the records state them, with one recommendation, ending with the sign-off it waits on. The architect's story read-back says whether the design serves the operator's intent; the lead's plan read-back says how the story will be built. At a session's start the architect's read-back carries the current design, then what is open, then the stories and tasks in flight, before anything is recorded or changed. A read-back held at a gate or called by the operator ends its holder's turn until the operator answers.
reason: The read-back was an ordering only, judged by whether it came before a change, so an architect read back and recorded in the same turn; it is now the handover at a gate, held by the architect for a story and by the lead for its plan.
